title: Load Balancing LLM Requests
summary: Distribute inference work using token demand, queue pressure, capability, and cache locality instead of treating all requests as equal.
overview: LLM load balancing assigns requests to compatible inference replicas or provider deployments. Request count is an inadequate load signal: a short classification and a long document analysis consume very different prefill, decoding, and key-value cache resources. A useful balancer estimates work while preserving fairness and admission limits.

The routing unit is normally a complete generation. Moving an active sequence requires engine-specific state transfer and should not be assumed. Prefix-aware routing may improve reuse, but excessive affinity can overload one replica while others remain idle. Balance locality against queueing delay using measured workload behavior.

production.poc: Start by comparing round-robin routing with observed prompt lengths and completion times.
production.production: Production adds bounded queues, token-aware concurrency, cancellation propagation, and separate interactive and background capacity.
production.scale: At scale, route across failure domains, account for heterogeneous accelerators, and test hot-prefix traffic and tenant fairness under sustained overload.

components.name: Request estimator
components.role: Estimates input tokens, output budget, required model, and deadline.

components.name: Replica directory
components.role: Publishes available model versions, health, and capacity classes.

components.name: Scheduling policy
components.role: Combines queue delay, token pressure, fairness, and optional prefix locality.

components.name: Admission queue
components.role: Bounds waiting work and rejects requests that cannot meet their deadlines.

components.name: Inference replicas
components.role: Report active tokens, cache pressure, completion, and cancellation.

flow.title: Classify work
flow.description: Resolve model compatibility and separate latency-sensitive traffic from deferred jobs.

flow.title: Estimate demand
flow.description: Count prompt tokens and use an explicit output ceiling to approximate sequence cost.

flow.title: Select replica
flow.description: Choose among healthy compatible replicas using current queue and memory pressure.

flow.title: Admit or defer
flow.description: Reserve capacity or return a clear overload response before an unbounded queue forms.

flow.title: Run generation
flow.description: Keep the sequence on its chosen replica and propagate caller cancellation promptly.

flow.title: Update estimates
flow.description: Compare predicted and actual cost so future routing reflects real request distributions.

useCase.title: Balancing interactive drafting and overnight summaries
useCase.situation: A document platform shares model capacity between interactive drafting and large workspace summaries.
useCase.problem: Long summary requests occupy cache and delay short user edits.
useCase.requirement: Protect interactive response time while using spare capacity for background work.
useCase.architecture: The gateway maintains separate queues and routes with token budgets and per-tenant fairness.
runtime: A short edit enters the interactive queue with a small output cap.
An overnight summary is admitted only when its capacity allocation is available.
useCase.failure: When one replica reports cache exhaustion, new long requests defer while active sequences finish safely.
useCase.impact: Evaluate tail latency by workload class, queue age, and accelerator utilization together; average throughput can hide interactive starvation.

tradeoffs.cost: Requires estimation and live engine metrics.
Creates hotspots if many requests share one prefix.
May leave capacity idle during uneven demand.

failures.detection: Requests accumulate on a replica that appears idle.
failures.recovery: Expire capacity advertisements and use conservative admission.

failures.detection: Background queue age rises despite available overall throughput.
failures.recovery: Reserve a minimum share and age waiting jobs fairly.

mistakes.fix: Include token and memory pressure in decisions.
Return bounded retry guidance or defer through a durable queue.
Release reservations and stop abandoned generations.

whenToUse: Use for multiple compatible inference replicas.
Use when prompt and output sizes vary substantially.
Use when interactive and batch workloads compete.
whenNotToUse: Avoid complex routing for one lightly loaded endpoint.
Do not move live sequences without supported state transfer.
Do not prioritize cache hits above authorization or deadlines.
checklist: Measure input and output length distributions.
Set queue and token admission limits.
Track cancelled work that still consumes compute.
